gap.behavioural_impact: In GOAT and Edison an attack by an opponent's Tribute Set monster (a Set Monarch or similar, later flipped) should let Blast Held by a Tribute wipe their face-up Attack Position monsters for 1000 damage; the shipped card refuses to activate against it.

review.notes:
CAUTION on the packet's upstream entry: upstream_implementations lists passcode 511005091 'Blast Held by a Tribute (Anime)' from cards-unofficial.cdb (script unofficial/c511005091.lua, annotated 'original script by Shad3'). That is an anime-only card with an entirely different effect - it is chosen when Set, tracks the monster Tributed for the opponent's Tribute Summon, and destroys that attacker for damage equal to its ATK - and its text_matches_version ratio against the lineage is 0.4723. It is NOT a period implementation of the TCG card and must not be reused as a baseline; hence the acknowledged-gap baseline and the conflicting-evidence flag. Chain starts at v0 (DCR-104, 2003-12-01), the text in force at both the 2005-04-01 GOAT and 2010-04-24 Edison snapshots, since the DT05 reprint is 2011-09-29. Trailing v1 -> v2 (DPRP-EN034, 2016-09-15) is the PSCT rewrite ('Destroy as many face-up Attack Position monsters they control as possible, and if you do, inflict 1000 damage'), matching the pinned cdb text; it conditionalises the burn on at least one destruction, which is standard PSCT formalisation, so it is not recorded as a behavioural change. No entry for this card in edison-functional-errata.md.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Blast Held by a Tribute). No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. Verdicts: [event] d1 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (DT05-EN099, Duel Terminal 5b)

event.historical_text: You can only activate this card when your opponent declares an attack with a monster on his/her side of the field that has been Tribute Summoned or Set. Destroy all face-up Attack Position monsters on your opponent's side of the field and inflict 1000 points of damage to your opponent's Life Points.
event.modern_text: Activate only when your opponent declares an attack with a Tribute Summoned monster they control. Destroy all face-up Attack Position monsters they control and inflict 1000 damage to your opponent.
event.summary: Functional erratum: the DCR-104 activation condition is an attack by an opponent's monster 'that has been Tribute Summoned or Set'; DT05-EN099 drops 'or Set', leaving only 'a Tribute Summoned monster they control'. In a period format an opponent's monster that was Tribute Set and later turned face-up still lets the Trap resolve; after the erratum only a Tribute Summoned attacker does.

rulings_check.difference: The era condition also covers an opponent's attacker that was Tribute Set (then flipped face-up); the modern condition covers only a Tribute Summoned attacker.
